title: Graceful degradation crediting and circuit hysteresis specification for conversational endpoints
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: Define a unified policy and implementation spec that assigns graceful-degradation credits to endpoints and model variants, and introduces circuit-breaker hysteresis behavior to reduce oscillation during multi-region failover and bursty conversational traffic. The outcome will be a deterministic crediting algorithm, config knobs for hysteresis and backoff, and an operational runbook for tuning and incident response.
background: We currently observe rapid circuit open/close oscillations during bursty chat traffic and regional failover events. This causes repeated degradations, customer confusion, and wasted error-budget churn. Existing SLOs are defined per endpoint but lack a mechanism for time-phased crediting or hysteresis-aware circuit controls that treat transient spikes differently from sustained regressions.
goals: Create a mathematically-specified graceful-degradation credit model that normalizes across token-length and route weight
Introduce circuit hysteresis parameters (open_threshold, cool_down_window, reopen_rate_multiplier) and document defaults for conversational routes
Provide per-variant credit allocation so pinned variants and cheaper fallbacks are accounted for in error-budget transfers
Produce a playbook (runbook) for SREs and on-call engineers to tune credits and circuit parameters during on-call incidents
Add observable signals and dashboards to validate credit burn behavior and hysteresis effectiveness
proposed_solution: SLI definition: Use 'successful_quality_tokens' / 'requested_tokens' as the primary SLI. A token is successful if response passes functional checks (no truncated outputs, no model error) AND the model's quality-score(probabilistic) >= 0.75 for eval set prompts. This makes SLOs quality-aware for conversational flows.

SLO expression: Maintain 99.5% quality-weighted token success over a rolling 30d window per endpoint. Secondary latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms for small-chat routes, p99 <= 600ms for long-form generation routes.

Credit model: Each endpoint has a daily 'degradation_credit' proportional to baseline qps and historical quality variance. Formula (human-readable): credit_daily = baseline_qps * baseline_token_length * baseline_error_tolerance_factor. Burn rate = observed_quality_deficit * request_token_count / credit_daily.

Per-variant allocation: Allocate credits to model variants via weighting vector W_variant = (cost_factor)^-1 * quality_alpha. This biases credits toward cheaper, high-quality variants and enables transparent fallback economics.

Circuit hysteresis: Implement three configurable params: open_threshold (burn_rate > X for Y minutes), cool_down_window (minimum time circuit remains open), reopen_rate_multiplier (exponential backoff multiplier applied to subsequent reopen attempts). Default values: open_threshold=0.25 (25% extra burn over budget sustained for 5m), cool_down_window=600s, reopen_rate_multiplier=2.0.

Failover semantics: During regional failover, global credit escrow can be borrowed with a capped multiplier up to 1.5x per region; borrowing triggers a higher hysteresis floor to avoid immediate reopen flapping when primary returns.

Load-shedding policy: Token-aware shedding that evicts long-context requests first, preserving short interactive requests. Eviction priority = (normalized_token_length ^ 1.25) * (route_priority_weight).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover crediting math and hysteresis boundaries with edge cases (sudden spike, slow leak, region eviction)
Staging rollout shows reduction in circuit open/close events by >= 60% during synthetic burst tests (load harness results in linked dashboard)
Dashboards display: credit balance, burn_rate, active_circuits, open_duration_histogram, per-variant_credit_usage
Runbook created and reviewed by SRE and Product with >= 2 approvals
Performance overhead of new checks < 2% p95 latency impact on critical route
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: endpoint.degradation_credit_balance - Alert if balance < 15% of daily allocation
Metric: circuit.open_events_per_minute - Alert if reopening_rate > 3 per 10m for any endpoint
Synthetic canary: daily smoke prompts evaluated against golden responses - alert on regression > 2%
Graph: regional_credit_borrow_pct across active regions to detect long-running escrow usage
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Implement credit accounting and hysteresis flags behind feature gates for a subset of internal test tenants (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (staging): Run load harness (conversational burst scenarios) with feature enabled; iterate on thresholds (1 week)
Phase 3 (gradual prod): Rollout to <10% traffic by target endpoint; monitor; increment every 24h if circuit-flap metrics improve (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Full default enable and deprecate old naive circuit logic (1 week + observation)
Rollback: instant disable feature flag reverts to legacy circuit behavior and reclaims borrowed credits
security_and_compliance: Credit accounting and borrowing logic touch tenant isolation and billing signals. We must ensure no cross-tenant leakage of credit metadata. KMS encryption and audit logs are required for credit transfer operations. Coordinate with Security team for review and add to compliance audit scope.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-calibrated reopen multiplier can prolong degradations - Mitigation: conservative default + automated rollback when escrow usage > 1.2x for 30m
Risk: Credit model complexity may be hard to explain to customers - Mitigation: provide a simplified per-tenant dashboard and a prose FAQ
Risk: Observability gaps under high load - Mitigation: add high-cardinality sampling and retention for critical signals only
